BJK Stink

By: Liz Fish | Commission

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A Rendering plant in prime agricultural land is polluting the air with the most gut rendering stench and causing major health issues and the community appeal to the authorities falls on deaf ears

Unique Selling Point:
Grootvlei and Greylingstad once known for its clean air and idyllic farmland has become a living hell for its residents. Having a braai in their gardens, a country wedding, or an outride on a horse they are buying from the stud farm is a gamble. If the wind is from the East they hide indoors and even then, they can’t escape the stench. The smell is described as worse than a decomposing rat, it’s more like a decomposing human said one resident. Others describe it as the smell of cat pee, and apart from the gut-wrenching smell it’s impacting their health severely and their businesses.
Migraines, increased sinus infections, Asthma, shortness of breath, constantly coughing, blood clots on the lungs plague the residents and no number of appeals to the authorities seem to make an impact.
The source of the stench is BJK – a rendering plant that trucks in chicken feathers, blood, fat and offal and converts it into animal proteins, oils and minerals and frozen products which they sell to the pet food industry. It’s a lucrative industry but the surrounding community are paying the price


Summary:
The Green scorpions acknowledge that BJK has been a problem for many years. BJK need to install a biological scrubber which is an industry standard for the volatile Organic compounds for Ammonia and sulphur dioxide and chlorine emissions, but BJK say it’s too expensive. Instead it seems they extended their chimneys, so they release these gasses higher into the atmosphere- all that’s done is spread the stench further.
The main shareholder is an exceptionally rich Brit called Danny Sawirj of the Leo Group who owns a similar plant in Penrith England. BJK Industries is Leo Group’s South African subsidiary. Ironically the UK plant is lauded as being a major contributor to renewable energy and is punted as an environmental green solution. Its highly profitable enterprise but faces similar issues. Residents in Halifax and Bradford have complained about the noise and smells emanating from the company's factories.
Apart from the stench the trucks transporting the chicken waste drip and spill and leaving trails of blood and guts on the roads. The waste is not transported in refrigerated trucks and decomposes enroute. Many of the roads these trucks use are dirt and BJK takes their time before they clean it up. The goo spilling from the trucks stinks and causes fly infestation. In Britian they have been prosecuted for similar violations- here nothing happens.
Its not only the people that are suffering it’s the livestock as well.
Trucks trundle the dirt roads all through the night and production never ceases. The stench can be smelt 20kms away depending on which way the wind is blowing. And over the years it got worse. Two years ago, the plant shut down for three weeks when two workers died in the plant from asphyxiation. The owners of the plant refuse to release the report to the community. But the shut down in production was a massive relief from the stench. Anecdotally, residents say when they leave the area for holidays elsewhere their health improves
The water on the neighbouring farms was tested by water department, but they refuse to release the results to the farmers. Independent tests show high levels of ecoli and ammonia – but why won’t the water department release the results?
Residents approached the CSIR and various Universities to monitor the air quality and analyses the emissions, but were told it cost R100 000 residents can’t raise that kind of money.


Extra Budget Items:
BJK Head office is in Cape Town and so the confront will require the presenter to fly in to Cape Town. The presenter must be able to understand Zulu as one of the central interviews must be conducted in Zulu. There is also a protest by the farmers on Human Rights day - Saturday 21st March so the presenter needs to be available over the weekend

Script:


Opening
Masa Kekana VO: A 17-year-old plant in the heart of this Mpumalanga farming community, processes the blood, feathers and offal of up to 23 million chickens - every week.
Residents say the smell is overwhelming. Carried by winds it affects more than 3,000 people living in and around Greylingstad, now used to the sight of chicken carcasses, blood and feathers strewn along back roads.
The culprit is called BJK Industries.
Stephen Burrows “There are solutions out there, measures they can take to address this problem properly …
Masa Kekana VO: What BJK produces is primarily used in pet food; a manufacturing process infamous for causing a stink.
The situation is so bad here, according to residents, they’ve taken to protests like this one – large for such a small community – to make their voices heard.
Upsound Carel Pienaar” It's not a matter of staff shortage. It’s simply not being done, in other words they don’t deem it important.
Masa Kekana VO: But this multinational claims to be doing everything possible to limit the impacts of its operations, and denies claims that it’s causing illness among residents. Where cause and effect are almost impossible to prove, are the people of Greylinstad fighting a losing battle?
Breath
Masa Kekana Link:We arrived early this morning on this beautiful farm,to clear skies and fresh air, and then the wind turned, and suddenly there was this awful smell, I am really struggling to describe that smell right now, but it's quite nauseating, and apparently this isn’t as bad as it usually gets
Masa Kekana VO: When this plant started operations close to 20 years ago, under a different company, - it was convicted of several environmental violations, namely offensive odour emissions, operating a waste disposal site without a permit and failing to provide safe working conditions.
Breath
Masa Kekana VO: In 2016, the plant was bought by a multinational called Leo Oils, which invested millions in upgrades to its South African subsidiary BJK- and ramping up production.
Masa Kekana VO: Despite the upgrades, many residents say the smell is as bad as ever.
Suzelle and Konrad Steyn, moved here, four years ago.
Suzelle Stein “If we knew about it, I don't think we would have moved here at all. Because that was the main thing why we moved actually from Witbank is for the clean air to start a family.
Masa Kekana: what's it like actually living here? I tried to escape to go to the car during interviews, but it just it follows you. How would you describe the smell?
Suzelle Stein: It's not a smell that you can’t hide away from.Sometimes it smells like urine… sometimes it smells like something’s dead and has been standing for weeks and weeks and weeks.
Masa Kekana VO: They say their health has steadily declined.
Masa Kekana: And how are you feeling today?
Suzelle Stein: We actually went away to the coast for almost two weeks and it was nice. We actually slept. We didn't stand up with headaches or tightness on the chest, and we came back last week. I'm sitting currently with the chest that's closed again. My husband battles with migraines constantly. ..and there's no medicine that actually takes the migraine away because the smell is still in the air.
Masa Kekana VO: Last Christmas, Suzelle’s health, took a dramatic turn.
Suzelle Stein: The 24th I went to the kitchen and I made coffee for us…And I just started feeling like something is just like my whole body is just going. And I collapsed. We went to the doctor when I got by and he told me that my sinuses were completely blocked. And the thing is, I never had sinus problems ever before.
Breather
Masa Kekana VO “while there is no proof of a causal link between the plant’s emissions and the illnesses, many of the people we spoke to - both young and old - described similar ailments: burning eyes, headaches, nausea, sinus congestion and difficulty breathing, all commonly associated, with exposure to some of the pollutants emitted by rendering plants like BJK’s.

Up Sound Carel Pienaar” My name is Carel Pienaar, and I represent Save Greylingstad from BJK”
Masa Kekana VO “Carel Pienaar is a councilor at Dipaleseng Municipality and is leading the fightback against BJK.
Carel Pienaar: We unfortunately can't do air emission test because air emission test is just so expensive to do. That's what why we came together today was not just to put pressure on BJK, but also on the authorities to enforce the licence conditions put air test stations up for us as a community.
Masa Kekana VO: International studies have linked rendering plants to increased stress, respiratory irritation, and fatigue — and even higher cancer risks… in surrounding communities.
BUT- there has been no equivalent studies in South Africa and, despite years of complaints, there’s no legislation specifically limiting pollutants or managing odour, at rendering plants. Instead, facilities themselves are left to manage and report on these emissions.
…Beat
John Coetzee:: This is not the right place for this type of factory
Breath
John Coetzee “You get shortness of breath, you get terrible headaches, your eyes burn your throat, and your nasal passages have terrible sinus
Masa Kekana VO: John Coetzee’s family has farmed here for more than 80 years. His farm is downstream from the plant.
John Coetzee: We actually pump the water from underground. We've got an aquifer, our water is very shallow. It's ten meters deep and then the percolation from the water that comes from BJK obviously goes into that water and it contaminates it.
Masa Kekana VO: After the plant was built, John’s cattle began aborting prematurely
John Coetzee: I've been working with cattle more than 50 years, so I think I'm qualified to realize when these is normal and not normal I took a fetus from cattle and then found out that they were problems as a result of bacterial infection.
Masa Kekana LINK: When John's animals started getting sick he suspected that it was from the contaminated water in the dam.
VO: He no longer uses the water from this borehole, and continues to conduct independent water tests, which still show high levels of ecoli and sewerage
John Coetzee Clip Right in the onset of the thing we went and hand-delivered objections. Filled the documents in, paid thousands of rands to various institutions to try and help us.
And then when you put your objection in, nobody comes back to you.
Masa Kekana VO: And that, says John, is why The Save Greylingstad from BJK group was started… to little effect.
Masa Kekana LINK: Some of the residents have resorted to picketing outside the BJK plant, this is out of sheer frustration and what they have called is a lack of transparency
Carel Pienaar: In my world, when people in the surrounding areas phone me and kids that sits in school, they, I have to dismiss school and send them home, because of runny noses and sinus issues, when the community reports those issues to me, then I'm not so sure that the best standards are being implemented.
Wonderboy Mbatha: Our issues with BJK is that with the bad smell
Masa Kekana VO: Wonderboy Mbatha is the spokesperson for a local movement representing the unemployed.
Wonderboy Mbatha “ Some of them, they have difficulty in breathing because …they are on asthma. And that smell it affects the way we we breathe in our daily life because we know that in the morning when we wake up most of the time we should inhale fresh air but what is no longer happening
Masa Kekana VO: BJK invited us to tour their plant, where we’re shown the entire production process by Managing Director, Ricardo Louw.
Upsound:Ricardo Louw: “This is the start of the production , essentially of the steam that we need to run our process”
To date no evidence of our process linked to health concerns have ever been reported or produced.
Masa Kekana VO: Waste from around 23 million chickens is diverted from landfills to this plant each week.
Blood, feathers and offal are cooked up and transformed into animal feed…
and oil is extracted for use in jet fuel.
Louw insists all licences are in place.
Masa Kekana: We've spoken to people who've moved to the area with no health problems or minimal health problems moved here. And the smell, let's be honest, it's unbearable and it's not just the human lives as well. There's also the animals that have been impacted
Ricardo Louw Unpleasant odours does not necessarily mean harmful exposure. So it's important to make the distinction. We actually do independent monitoring on site where we get occupational hygiene specialists in, um, who then bring in their own equipment.
Masa Kekana VO: Louw says millions have been invested in upgrades in the past decade.
Ricardo Louw: We ensure that the permeate or the clean water, after taking it through our purification plant, conforms to those standards. Multiple sources can contribute to water pollution. It is a sign it should be assessed scientifically and not by assumptions by looking upstream
Masa Kekana VO: Residents also complain that waste brought in by unrefrigerated trucks is frequently dropped, on farm backroads creating a festering trail, sometimes running for kms.
Louw admits there’ve been some incidents, but insists, there’ve been significant investments in ensuring the trailers are leak protected.
These recent pictures suggest otherwise.
Breath
Masa Kekana VO After our interview and under strict conditions, BJK showed us the results of a 48-hour monitoring exercise conducted inside the facility, and along its immediate perimeter, to determine the concentration of airborne pollutants. It found that ammonia and aldehyde concentrations were low at the BJK facility
However, in the report it stated if there were ongoing odour complaints, air monitoring would need to be conducted at various locations. International studies show, that monitoring needs to happen over an extended period of time - at various locations- for a fuller picture.
We weren’t allowed to film the report, and its contents haven’t been shared with the community.
Ricardo Louw: We can certainly see what is the best way to do it and who to publish it to. We certainly not going to send it to 1 or 2 individuals who have been pushing for it.
Carel Pienaar” So this is the memorandum
Carel Pienaar : When these tests get done, make the results known to the public. It should not be hidden. Tell us what's going on. Tell us what's being done.
Masa Kekana VO:In the absence of specific emissions legislation, residents here can only rely on their Constitutional right to a healthy environment in their battle with a multinational. But, even then, the uncertainty around cause and effect will muddy the waters.

Promo 1: Between the cosmos and cattle, there's something foul in the air.. “You get shortness of breath, you get terrible headaches, your eyes burn your throat, and your nasal passages have terrible sinus
But is a local chicken rendering plant causing more than just a big stink?

Promo 2
VO: They came seeking an escape from the big city
It's not a smell that you can’t hide away from. Sometimes it smells like urine… sometimes it smells like something’s dead and has been standing for weeks and weeks and weeks.
VO: The dream of a rural paradise - but the reality... stinks

Promo 3: Residents fight back at a multinational animal processing plant
“Some of them, they have difficulty in breathing because …they are on asthma. And that smell it affects the way we we breathe in our daily life because we know that in the morning when we wake up most of the time we should inhale fresh air but what is no longer happening. Where cause and effect are almost impossible to prove, are the people of Greylinstad fighting a losing battle.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A Rendering plant in prime agricultural land is polluting the air with the most gut rendering stench and causing major health issues and the community appeal to the authorities falls on deaf ears
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Grootvlei and Greylingstad once known for its clean air and idyllic farmland has become a living hell for its residents. Having a braai in their gardens, a country wedding, or an outride on a horse they are buying from the stud farm is a gamble. If the wind is from the East they hide indoors and even then, they can’t escape the stench. The smell is described as worse than a decomposing rat, it’s more like a decomposing human said one resident. Others describe it as the smell of cat pee, and apart from the gut-wrenching smell it’s impacting their health severely and their businesses. Migraines, increased sinus infections, Asthma, shortness of breath, constantly coughing, blood clots on the lungs plague the residents and no number of appeals to the authorities seem to make an impact. The source of the stench is BJK – a rendering plant that trucks in chicken feathers, blood, fat and offal and converts it into animal proteins, oils and minerals and frozen products which they sell to the pet food industry. It’s a lucrative industry but the surrounding community are paying the price
metadata.Summary: The Green scorpions acknowledge that BJK has been a problem for many years. BJK need to install a biological scrubber which is an industry standard for the volatile Organic compounds for Ammonia and sulphur dioxide and chlorine emissions, but BJK say it’s too expensive. Instead it seems they extended their chimneys, so they release these gasses higher into the atmosphere- all that’s done is spread the stench further. The main shareholder is an exceptionally rich Brit called Danny Sawirj of the Leo Group who owns a similar plant in Penrith England. BJK Industries is Leo Group’s South African subsidiary. Ironically the UK plant is lauded as being a major contributor to renewable energy and is punted as an environmental green solution. Its highly profitable enterprise but faces similar issues. Residents in Halifax and Bradford have complained about the noise and smells emanating from the company's factories. Apart from the stench the trucks transporting the chicken waste drip and spill and leaving trails of blood and guts on the roads. The waste is not transported in refrigerated trucks and decomposes enroute. Many of the roads these trucks use are dirt and BJK takes their time before they clean it up. The goo spilling from the trucks stinks and causes fly infestation. In Britian they have been prosecuted for similar violations- here nothing happens. Its not only the people that are suffering it’s the livestock as well. Trucks trundle the dirt roads all through the night and production never ceases. The stench can be smelt 20kms away depending on which way the wind is blowing. And over the years it got worse. Two years ago, the plant shut down for three weeks when two workers died in the plant from asphyxiation. The owners of the plant refuse to release the report to the community. But the shut down in production was a massive relief from the stench. Anecdotally, residents say when they leave the area for holidays elsewhere their health improves The water on the neighbouring farms was tested by water department, but they refuse to release the results to the farmers. Independent tests show high levels of ecoli and ammonia – but why won’t the water department release the results? Residents approached the CSIR and various Universities to monitor the air quality and analyses the emissions, but were told it cost R100 000 residents can’t raise that kind of money.
